profile.headline: Software Engineer at Meta
profile.summary:
Tech lead supporting iOS Top of Newsfeed Infra code in the Facebook app.

Past: Leading teams that are building new mobile products.  Built the iOS and Android Publisher SDKs for Criteo (API Design is Hard).

Further Past: Solving for ITP, Facebook Ad Buying stack, User Identity and Event Tracking at scale, iOS Developer, Platform Engineer, Data Warehouse Developer, Reluctant DBA

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Tech lead supporting Stories and Reels Top of Newsfeed Infra in the iOS Facebook app

positions.title: Staff Software Engineering Lead
positions.description: Manager supporting a team of 6 iOS and Android engineers building Criteo's Mobile Advertising SDKs

positions.title: Senior Software Engineering Lead
positions.description: Mobile Identity Solutions, Facebook Ad-Buying Backend

positions.title: Senior Mobile Developer, R&D
positions.description: Maintain and scale backend that captures over 2.5 billion events per day for over 20,000 clients.  Specialized event tracking solutions dedicated to safari.  User-Agent parsing at scale.  Designed, developed, and shipped our mobile Advertiser SDK (iOS and Android).

positions.title: Software Engineer (iOS Apps)
positions.description:
Individual contributor to SafeZone for iOS, Fixmo's flagship secure container product.

Principal maintainer of 3 Super Safe for iOS.  3 Super Safe is an OTA backup and restore solution offered in the Hong Kong market by 3 Hong Kong and operated by Fixmo.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: Backend (C# + SQL) and iOS engineer building cross-platform over-the-air backup and restore of your smartphone.

positions.title: DBA
positions.description:
Assumed DBA responsibilities after developing our next-generation data warehouse and reporting portal using Netezza and Logi XML.

Assumed responsibility for database architecture and administration after demonstrating key competencies in database design and management during data warehouse implementation. Responsible for a >6 terabyte MS SQL Server footprint in Fisher Plaza, Seattle, as well as high-speed operational systems in New Jersey.

positions.title: Software Developer II
positions.description:
Advanced to Software Developer II after demonstrating key successes with the creation of our first Real-Time Reporting offering.

Rapid, problem oriented development of high-performance middle-tier messaging solutions. Developed key reporting software for two generations of our data warehouse and reporting portal. Designed and developed a C# implementation of our in-house software development framework to ease the transition to .NET for our principal software developers. Extensive cross-discipline coding, design and maintenance tasks using MS SQL Server, C#, ASP.Net, and C/C++.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: Rapid, fast paced development of large scale, data oriented messaging and reporting platforms for SMS and MMS.

positions.title: Network Administrator
positions.description:
Advanced to a local role as a Network Administrator in Bellevue office upon demonstration of exceptional technical skill and passion for information technology.

Member of a three person helpdesk and networking team that covered over 100 on-site users and over 1900 contingent staff.  Managed all major enterprise services, including Exchange, Backup, Storage, and Disaster Recovery.

Designed and implemented laptop inventory management system for company executives to provide clear insight and direction on stock deployed with over 1900 contingent staff in the Redmond area.  Statistics on equipment age, failure rates, and cost amortization helped the executive team make informed, timely decisions about equipment budgets and purchasing.

positions.title: Technical Specialist
positions.description:
Provided pre-event and onsite IT deployments for major Microsoft events.

Operated on tight schedules to transport, deploy and manage large scale network, server and desktop implementations anywhere in the world.  Implementations were typically built in less than 7 days, and often consisted of more than 1000 machines deployed across massive conference and trade centers.
